prompts.display_text: Pin a country with 500 or more Church congregations (wards and branches, end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: Pin a country with 500 or more Church congregations (wards and branches, end of 2025).
prompts.note: Next below the line: Guatemala (441) and DR Congo (431).
prompts.summary: At the end of 2025 the United States had about 14,600 Church congregations (wards and branches). Brazil, Mexico and the Philippines followed, and Nigeria had about 880, many of them small. Canada just made the 500 mark with 501.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: About 14,600 congregations.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: About 2,000 congregations.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: 501 congregations, just over the line.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: About 1,900 congregations.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: About 1,370 congregations.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: About 740 congregations.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: About 580 congregations.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: About 880 congregations, many of them small.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: About 810 congregations.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where Saints vol. 3 or Global Histories record Ezra Taft Benson's 1946 postwar relief visit.
prompts.text_original: In 1946 apostle Ezra Taft Benson presided over the European Mission and traveled widely to deliver Church relief and reorganize branches after World War II. Pin a country where Saints vol. 3 chapter 32 or the Global Histories place him that year.
prompts.citation: Saints vol. 3 ch. 32; Global Histories chronologies
prompts.note: Norway, France and Czechoslovakia got 1946 aid, but no record places Benson there, so they do not count.
prompts.summary: Ezra Taft Benson arrived in Europe early in 1946 to oversee Church relief for Saints hit by World War II. He traveled from London to Germany, Austria, the Low Countries, Scandinavia and Switzerland, and won visas to reach Saints in Poland. He also rededicated Finland for missionary work.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Directed about 2,500 tons of Church aid; visited the Berlin mission home.

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: Reorganized the Austrian District in March 1946; saw Vienna.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Oversaw food and clothing distribution, spring 1946.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Saw the ruins of war from London, mission headquarters (saints-v3:32).

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: Organized relief distribution in Rotterdam, May 1946.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: Visited Antwerp and Liege, April 1946.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: Visited Copenhagen branches, February 1946.

answers.name: Poland
answers.fact: Reached Zelwagi in August 1946 after a long struggle for visas.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: Saints vol. 3 says he saw Stockholm on his travels.

answers.name: Finland
answers.fact: Rededicated Finland for preaching at Larsmo, July 16, 1946.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding land allotted to a tribe of Israel in Joshua 13-19
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding land allotted to a tribe of Israel in Joshua 13-19, from Bashan and Gilead east of the Jordan to Asher's border at great Zidon and Judah's border at the river of Egypt
prompts.note: Jericho, Bethel and Hebron are in the West Bank (Palestine); much of Judah and the northern tribes lie in Israel.
prompts.summary: After the conquest, Joshua divided the land by lot. Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh took Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan, while the other tribes took Canaan, with Asher's coast stretching toward Zidon and Tyre and Judah's south border reaching the river of Egypt (Josh 13-19).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Most tribes, including Naphtali, Zebulun, Issachar and much of Judah, were given land west of the Jordan (Josh 15-19).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Benjamin, Ephraim and Judah held land now in the West Bank, such as Jericho, Bethel and Hebron (Josh 15:54; 16:1; 18:21-22).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh received Gilead and the plains east of the Jordan (Josh 13:8-25).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Asher's border reached to great Zidon and the strong city Tyre (Josh 19:28-29).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Half of Manasseh received all Bashan, the kingdom of Og with Edrei and Ashtaroth (Josh 13:12, 29-31).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Judah's south border went out unto the river of Egypt, the Wady el Arish in northern Sinai (Josh 15:4, 47; Bible Dictionary).

prompts.display_text: Pin a European country where a current General Authority Seventy once led a mission (as of October 2026).
prompts.text_original: As of October 2026, several General Authority Seventies had led missions in Europe as mission presidents. Pin a European country where one of those missions was headquartered, as named in the Church's official biographies.
prompts.summary: Many General Authority Seventies first led missions. As of October 2026, they had led European missions in England, France, Spain, Portugal, Germany, Russia, Ukraine, the Czech Republic and Slovakia, and Slovenia and Croatia. Elder Jorg Klebingat, born in Germany, presided in Kyiv, Ukraine.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: England London Mission (Elder Sinclair) and England Manchester Mission (Elder Peter M. Johnson).

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Elder Michael Cziesla was interim president of the Germany Frankfurt Mission in 2020.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Spain Barcelona Mission (Elder Villar).

answers.name: France
answers.fact: France Lyon Mission (Elder Giraud-Carrier).

answers.name: Portugal
answers.fact: Elder Ronald M. Barcellos was called as a mission leader in Portugal in 2021.

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: Elder Paul B. Pieper and his wife were mission leaders in St. Petersburg.

answers.name: Ukraine
answers.fact: Ukraine Kyiv Mission (Elder Klebingat).

answers.name: Czech Republic
answers.fact: Czech/Slovak Mission, based in Prague, 2013 to 2016 (Elder McConkie).

answers.name: Croatia
answers.fact: The Slovenia/Croatia Mission that Elder Rowe led from 2011 also covered Croatia.

answers.name: Slovakia
answers.fact: The Czech/Slovak Mission that Elder McConkie led, 2013 to 2016, also covered Slovakia.

answers.name: Slovenia
answers.fact: Elder Edward B. Rowe was called in 2011 to lead the Slovenia/Croatia Mission, based in Ljubljana.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Latin American mainland country whose first General Authority from that country was called between 1981 and 1991
prompts.text_original: In the 1980s Latin American members began to be called as General Authorities. A Latin American mainland country (Mexico, Central America or Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking South America) whose first native General Authority was called between 1981 and 1991.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (Latin American mainland); Church News 1989, 1991 and 2021
prompts.note: Later firsts include Uruguay (Francisco J. Vinas, 1996), Venezuela (Rafael E. Pino, 2008) and Peru (Juan A. Uceda, 2010).
prompts.summary: Angel Abrea of Argentina became the first General Authority from South America in 1981. Brazil followed in 1985, Mexico and Guatemala in 1989 as the Second Quorum of the Seventy was formed, Chile in 1990 and Colombia in 1991. Each call showed the Church's leadership growing with its Latin American membership.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Horacio A. Tenorio, the first General Authority of Mexican ancestry, was sustained to the Second Quorum of the Seventy, April 1, 1989.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Angel Abrea was called to the First Quorum of the Seventy in April 1981, the first General Authority from South America.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Helio da Rocha Camargo was called as a General Authority Seventy, April 6, 1985.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: Eduardo Ayala became the first Chilean General Authority Seventy, March 31, 1990.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Carlos H. Amado was called as a General Authority Seventy, April 1, 1989.

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: Julio E. Davila, Colombia's first stake president, was sustained to the Second Quorum of the Seventy, April 6, 1991, the first General Authority from Colombia.
